items.title: 2 month player review
items.summary:
Gacha system might look weird at 90 pity. You are guaranteed an ssr every 30 pulls and 30% it will be the featured character. BUT the game throws pulls at you.

A few weeks ago, I already got all 5 teams I needed for the endgame mode, and I get 380/500 points. Remaining rewards aren’t significant to miss out on. That explains the game’s gacha system on its own.
items.author: Severelag

items.title: A genuinely underrated game
items.summary:
I started playing Morimens recently and honestly didn’t expect to get this invested in it. At first, the amount of different systems and mechanics felt a little overwhelming, and the game definitely takes some time to understand. But once I started getting the hang of the deck-building and team synergies, I really began to enjoy it.

What surprised me the most, though, was the story and lore. The world feels genuinely interesting and mysterious, and I found myself wanting to learn more about what is actually happening and who these characters are. The characters themselves are also very well written, and their designs feel genuinely unique compared to many other gacha games. They all have their own distinct personalities, which makes it surprisingly easy to become attached to them and become invested in their stories.

Even though most of the story is not fully voiced, I still found myself becoming genuinely invested in both the characters and the story. The writing, atmosphere and character interactions manage to carry a lot of the emotional weight on their own, which says a lot about how well the characters are written. I do hope that more parts of the story will receive voice acting in the future, because I think it would make the experience even better.

I’m still a relatively new player, so I can’t speak for every aspect of the endgame yet, but my experience so far has been genuinely positive. The game isn’t perfect, and some of the systems could probably be explained better for new players, but overall I think Morimens deserves a lot more attention than it gets.

I’m honestly really glad that I discovered Morimens, because I probably would have completely missed it otherwise. It still feels like a game that isn’t very well known, which is surprising considering how much it has to offer. I genuinely hope more people discover it in the future, because I think it deserves a much larger audience.

If you enjoy darker fantasy, Lovecraftian themes, interesting lore, well-written characters and strategic card-based gameplay, I would definitely recommend giving it a try.
